Q: Process.Start can't access Roblox protocol A:

Process.Start can't access roblox-player:// protocol Fix: Use UseShellExecute = true Process.Start(new ProcessStartInfo { FileName = "roblox-player://placeId=123456", UseShellExecute = true }); Also make sure: Roblox is installed properly Protocol is registered (reinstall Roblox if needed) That’s it

Q: Does `ext4` use `i_generation` inside `name_to_handle_at`? A:

Prologue

Even though I'm mostly interested in ext-based file-systems (and specifically ext4), I'll try to answer this as broadly as I can (took me an hour of looking into the linux-kernel & [disclamer] a few prompts to grasp how precisely and mostly works... Therefore, since it took me quit a while, I decided to share it so it potentially helps others in the future, too... + because I wanted a place to gather all those infos I collected)

Answer

Yes, a curated\abstract idea of how name_to_handle_at actually does that internally, goes like this:

  1. name_to_handle_at syscall (user-space entry point)
  2. do_sys_name_to_handle() in fs/fhandle.c (syscall handler)
  3. exportfs_encode_fh() in fs/exportfs/expfs.c (generic encoding dispatcher)
  4. exportfs_encode_inode_fh() in fs/exportfs/expfs.c (gets the filesystem-specific operations)
  5. nop->encode_fh(...) (filesystem-specific callback, e.g., generic_encode_ino32_fh for ext4)
  6. File handle populated with i_generation, i_ino, and parent info

Practicly you have at linux/fs/fhandle.c -> name_to_handle_at calling do_sys_name_to_handle which in turn calls linux/fs/exportfs/expfs.c -> exportfs_encode_fh calling exportfs_encode_inode_fh where const struct export_operations *nop = inode->i_sb->s_export_op; gets the apropriate operations (for the file-system in which the inode belongs to [e.g. generic_encode_ino32_fh for ext4]) finally used at nop->encode_fh(...) to populate the file-handle with i_generation + etc.

(for file systems that don't belong to the "generic encoding dispatcher" you may look for ..._encode_fh) (Now if you ask me how or where inodes end up with i_sb->s_export_op idk... haven't looked that deep)

  • Why do we need to change files i_generation number?

Q: create dictionary from json A:

As said by dbc, you can use a dictionary just like JSON: public class public class Lines { public Dictionary<string, Line> lines { get; set; } = new(); }. The property names (here "0010" and "0020") will become the keys. This works with both System.Text.Json and Newtonsoft.
